role_sought: Member of the Knesset, Likud list (fifth place)
detail: First election to the Knesset, on the Likud list led by Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir; Likud formed a national unity government with Labor. The Knesset's own results pages are not reachable from outside Israel (geo-blocked), so figures are taken from the Wikipedia summary of the official results.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset, Likud list
detail: Likud lost power to Yitzhak Rabin's Labor Party; Netanyahu was re-elected.

opponent: David Levy, Benny Begin, Moshe Katsav
detail: First direct election of the Likud leader by party members, to succeed Yitzhak Shamir.

election: 1996 election for Prime Minister (first direct election)
detail: Held with the Knesset election under the 1992 direct-election law; he won by about one percentage point, while Labor won more Knesset seats than the joint Likud–Gesher–Tzomet list. He formed a government on 18 June 1996.
Lost to Ehud Barak; he then resigned from the Knesset and the Likud leadership.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset, Likud list
detail: Likud, led by Ariel Sharon, won the election; Netanyahu returned to the Knesset and became finance minister.

vote_share: 44.4% (Wikipedia's article on the primary; its article on Netanyahu gives 47%)
detail: Held after Ariel Sharon left Likud to found Kadima. Sources differ on the exact percentage.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Likud's worst result to date; Netanyahu became Leader of the Opposition.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Likud finished one seat behind Kadima, but President Shimon Peres asked Netanyahu to form the government, which was sworn in on 31 March 2009 with Yisrael Beiteinu, Shas, Labor and others.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; head of the joint Likud Yisrael Beiteinu list
detail: The joint list came first but fell short of expectations; he formed a coalition with Yesh Atid, HaTnua and several smaller parties.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
opponent: Zionist Union (Isaac Herzog, Tzipi Livni): 24 seats
detail: Likud won a larger margin than polls predicted.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Coalition talks failed over ultra-Orthodox conscription and the Knesset dissolved itself, triggering a new election. The Central Elections Committee's results site for this election no longer answers, so figures come from the Wikipedia summary.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
opponent: Blue and White (Benny Gantz, Yair Lapid): 25.95% (1,151,214 votes), 33 seats
detail: Official final results of the Central Elections Committee: turnout 69.83% of 6,394,030 registered voters. Neither bloc could form a government.
Held a month after his indictment was announced.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
result: Elected; remained Prime Minister under a rotation agreement
opponent: Blue and White (Benny Gantz): 26.59% (1,220,381 votes), 33 seats
detail: Official final results of the Central Elections Committee: turnout 71.52%. In April 2020 Gantz agreed to an emergency unity government under Netanyahu with a rotation of the premiership after 18 months, which did not take place.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
result: Elected; lost office to the Bennett–Lapid coalition
detail: Official final results of the Central Elections Committee: turnout 67.44%. Likud came first, but Netanyahu and his allies fell short of a majority, and a coalition led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid took office in June 2021.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
detail: Official final results of the Central Elections Committee: turnout 70.63% of 6,788,804 registered voters. Netanyahu's bloc of Likud, Religious Zionism–Otzma Yehudit (14 seats), Shas (11) and United Torah Judaism (7) won 64 of 120 seats; the government was sworn in on 29 December 2022.
Likud members chose the party's Knesset slate; the top places went to Netanyahu, Eli Cohen and Amir Ohana.

role_sought: Member of the Knesset; Likud leader and candidate for Prime Minister
result: Pending: the vote is scheduled for 27 October 2026
opponent: Main challengers: Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) and Naftali Bennett (Together)
detail: The first Knesset election held on its legally scheduled date since 1988. Polls reported by the Times of Israel in July 2026 showed Netanyahu and his allies well short of a majority. Official results are due to be confirmed on 4 November 2026.
